problems.title: Campus Knowledge Agent
problems.problem: Students waste hours searching for circulars, syllabi, exam timetables, and department notices scattered across PDFs, WhatsApp groups, and notice boards.
problems.challenge: Build an AI assistant that ingests institutional documents and answers student queries in natural language. Every answer must cite its source document.
problems.deliverable: Upload 5+ PDFs and get a chat interface with grounded answers and source citations. Documents and vector embeddings are stored in MongoDB Atlas.
problems.stretch: Tamil/English bilingual answers, an 'I don't know' fallback when the answer is not in the documents, and admin analytics on the most-asked questions.

problems.title: Smart Complaint Triage for Civic Bodies
problems.problem: Municipal grievance portals receive thousands of unstructured complaints, often with photos. These are sorted and routed by hand, which causes long delays.
problems.challenge: Build a system that takes a complaint as text and/or image, classifies its category and urgency, extracts the location, detects duplicates, and routes it to the right department.
problems.deliverable: A submission form with multimodal classification using Gemini vision and text, an auto-assigned department and priority score, and a dashboard showing complaints by category.
problems.stretch: Merging duplicate complaints, an interactive map heatmap view, and SLA breach alerts.

problems.title: Accessibility Auditor for Campus & Civic Websites
problems.problem: Most college and municipal websites fail basic accessibility standards — poor contrast, missing alt text, unlabeled form fields — locking out visually or motor-impaired users, and manual audits are slow and rarely repeated.
problems.challenge: Build a tool that scans a given webpage (URL or uploaded HTML) and flags concrete violations with the exact element at fault, plus a ready-to-use fix for each.
problems.deliverable: URL/HTML input, automated detection for 3 violation categories (alt text, contrast, form labels), a report listing each violation with its element and severity, and a Gemini-generated fix suggestion per violation, logged to MongoDB.
problems.stretch: A 4th violation category (heading structure), a before/after live preview applying fixes, and a downloadable patch file.

problems.title: Cross-Hospital Resource Rebalancer
problems.problem: Existing bed/oxygen/ventilator dashboards only show each hospital's own stock in isolation — nobody looks across hospitals in the same district to notice that Hospital A is about to run short while Hospital B has spare capacity sitting idle.
problems.challenge: Using a small simulated live feed (5–6 hospitals, one resource type e.g. oxygen cylinders, updated every few seconds), build a system that predicts which hospital will run short within the next few hours using a lightweight trend model, and simultaneously recommends a specific transfer (from which hospital, how much, by when) to prevent it — turning prediction into an actionable redistribution plan, not just a warning.
problems.deliverable: Simulated multi-hospital resource stream written to MongoDB → simple trend-based shortage predictor per hospital (e.g., linear depletion rate) with a visible confidence/accuracy check against held-out simulated data → dashboard showing live stock per hospital, predicted time-to-shortage, and a ranked transfer recommendation → Gemini-generated one-line justification per recommendation ('Move 40 units from B to A — B has 6hrs surplus, A depletes in 2hrs').
problems.stretch: Multi-resource tracking (beds + oxygen), automated distance-aware transit routing, and emergency escalation alerts.

problems.title: Phishing Shield
problems.problem: Phishing through SMS, email, and fake payment links is the leading cause of digital fraud in India. First-time internet users are the most vulnerable.
problems.challenge: Build a tool that analyses a suspicious message, URL, or screenshot and returns a risk verdict with a simple explanation of why it is dangerous.
problems.deliverable: Input as text, URL, or screenshot. Output is a risk score plus the red flags found (domain age, lookalike domains, urgency language). Every scan is logged to MongoDB.
problems.stretch: A browser extension or WhatsApp-style share target, a community-reported scam database, and regional-language explanations.

problems.title: Secure Passwordless Login Kit
problems.problem: Small web apps built by startups and college teams still rely on weak password-only authentication vulnerable to brute force and credential stuffing.
problems.challenge: Build a drop-in authentication module supporting passwordless login through magic links, OTP, or passkeys/WebAuthn, with rate limiting, session management, and suspicious-login detection.
problems.deliverable: A working demo app using the module, deployed on cloud hosting, with at least one passwordless method, brute-force protection, and a login activity log.
problems.stretch: Role-based access control (RBAC), new-device and new-location alerts, and clear developer documentation for quick SDK integration.

problems.title: Log Sentinel: AI-Assisted Threat Detection
problems.problem: Small organisations generate server logs but have no dedicated security operations team to monitor them, leaving intrusions undetected for weeks.
problems.challenge: Build a system that ingests web server or auth logs, detects anomalies such as brute-force attempts, SQL injection patterns, and unusual access, and summarises incidents in plain language.
problems.deliverable: Log upload or streaming, rule-based plus ML anomaly detection, an incident dashboard, and Gemini-written incident summaries with suggested remediation steps.
problems.stretch: Timeline reconstruction of an attack, automated email alerts, and mapping to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

problems.title: Tamper-Proof Academic Credential Verification
problems.problem: Fake degree certificates are a persistent recurring problem, and verifying credentials manually with universities is slow, costly, and unreliable.
problems.challenge: Build a DApp where institutions issue certificates whose cryptographic hashes are stored on-chain. Employers can verify any certificate instantly through a QR code or file upload.
problems.deliverable: A smart contract deployed on a public testnet (Sepolia or Polygon Amoy), an institution issuing portal, and a public verification page that instantly flags tampered files.
problems.stretch: On-chain revocation support, bulk batch issuance, and soulbound non-transferable tokens (SBTs) for credentials.

problems.title: Farm-to-Fork Supply Chain Tracker
problems.problem: Consumers cannot reliably verify the origin or authenticity of produce labelled organic or locally sourced, and farmers receive little financial credit for high quality.
problems.challenge: Build a supply-chain transparency system where each stage, from farmer to aggregator to transporter to retailer, records a cryptographic handoff on-chain. Consumers scan a QR code to see the product's journey.
problems.deliverable: A smart contract for product batches and handoffs, role-based stakeholder interfaces, and a consumer QR scan page rendering the verified timeline.
problems.stretch: Off-chain storage of metadata and images in MongoDB Atlas or IPFS, and direct micro-tipping or payment options to the original farmer.

problems.title: Transparent Donation & Fund Tracking
problems.problem: Donors to NGOs, college clubs, and disaster relief funds often have zero visibility into how their monetary contributions are actually disbursed and spent.
problems.challenge: Build a DApp where donations and expenditures are recorded on-chain, funds are released only on verified milestone approval, and donors can trace their exact contribution.
problems.deliverable: Donations via testnet tokens, milestone-based fund release through a verified smart contract, and a public transparency ledger dashboard.
problems.stretch: Multi-signature governance approval for fund releases, proof-of-spend uploads (receipts/photos), and automated donor impact reports.

problems.title: Decentralized Freelance Escrow
problems.problem: Freelancers and clients frequently encounter disputes over milestone delivery, scope changes, and delayed payment releases.
problems.challenge: Build a smart-contract-based freelance platform where project payment is locked in escrow up front and released deterministically according to predefined milestones.
problems.deliverable: Project creation, milestone definition, escrow deposit, work submission, employer approval, and programmatic payment release.
problems.stretch: Dispute resolution workflow, multi-signature decentralized arbitration, and on-chain operator reputation records.

problems.title: Smart Expense Companion for Students & Gig Workers
problems.problem: Students and gig economy workers face irregular incomes and limited financial literacy, leading to poor budgeting and lack of savings tracking.
problems.challenge: Build a personal finance app that auto-categorizes expenses from SMS text, receipts, or manual entry, forecasts the month-end balance, and delivers personalized savings advice.
problems.deliverable: Expense entry including receipt image parsing via Gemini, auto-categorization, a spending breakdown dashboard, and a predictive month-end balance forecast.
problems.stretch: A conversational 'Can I afford this?' conversational assistant, savings goals with behavioral nudges, and budgeting tailored for irregular income spikes.

problems.title: Multi-Agent Portfolio Rebalancer
problems.problem: Individual retail investors cannot react to live market shifts fast enough to keep their portfolio aligned with their risk tolerance, and manual rebalancing is slow, error-prone, and reactive.
problems.challenge: Build a council of collaborating agents — one that scrapes/streams live market data, one that evaluates the user's risk tolerance and target allocation, and one that computes and executes rebalancing trades — coordinating through MongoDB as shared state, with the council converging on a final rebalancing decision.
problems.deliverable: Live market data ingestion via web scraping into MongoDB → risk-tolerance agent producing a target allocation profile → rebalancing agent generating trade actions to close allocation gaps → council/coordinator logic merging all three agents' outputs into one decision → evaluation dashboard reporting decision latency and drift rebalancing accuracy per run.
problems.stretch: What-if macro shock stress testing, historical backtesting harness, and real-time Discord/Telegram trade alerts.

problems.title: SME Cash Flow Forecasting
problems.problem: Small businesses frequently make critical operational decisions without a clear forward-looking view of their near-term cash position, leading to sudden liquidity crises.
problems.challenge: Build a forecasting system that analyses historical sales, operational expenses, pending invoices, and payment patterns to reliably estimate future cash flow.
problems.deliverable: Dataset ingestion, an algorithmic cash-flow forecast, an income/expense dashboard, and automated low-cash threshold alerts.
problems.stretch: Interactive 'What-If' scenarios, delayed-payment impact simulation, and Gemini-generated strategic business recommendations.

problems.title: Disaster Response Coordination Platform
problems.problem: During emergencies and natural disasters, information about incidents, supplies, volunteers, and SOS calls is fragmented across uncoordinated communication channels.
problems.challenge: Build an integrated platform that collects incident reports and intelligently matches urgent relief requests with available resources and nearby responders.
problems.deliverable: Incident reporting portal, multimodal classification, priority triage assignment, resource matching engine, and an operational coordination dashboard.
problems.stretch: Multilingual SOS reporting, duplicate incident deduplication, live interactive geospatial map visualization, and Gemini-generated situational briefing summaries.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to participate in HACK_NEXUS 1.0?
faqs.a: Participation is open to all enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students from any recognized university or college. Every squad has exactly 3 operators; inter-departmental and inter-year squads are highly encouraged.

faqs.q: Can we use pre-existing codebases or templates?
faqs.a: All core problem logic must be authored entirely during the 10-hour clean sprint. Standard open-source libraries, open UI components, and framework scaffolds (Next.js, FastAPI, Vite, etc.) are fully allowed.

faqs.q: What physical amenities and computing hardware are provided?
faqs.a: Dedicated team desks in the CAR Lab (2nd Floor, Anna Block, Main Campus) with high-speed internet connectivity, uninterrupted power rails, round-the-clock coffee and refreshments.

faqs.q: How does the final pitch and valedictory evaluation operate?
faqs.a: Each squad receives a strict 5-minute live prototype demonstration, followed by a 2-minute technical architectural Q&A with the industry panel. Working deployments on cloud qualify for track points.

faqs.q: Will the 10-hour timer pause for lunch or refreshments?
faqs.a: No. The 10-hour sprint timer runs continuously without stoppage throughout the hackathon.lunch and continuous refreshments will be provided.

Squads can integrate partner technologies including Google Gemini (multimodal AI reasoning), MongoDB Atlas (vector search & operational state), Render Cloud (deployment), Web3 smart contracts, and Multi-Agent frameworks to power their solutions.
